claim_approval_lock_resolution.next_charter: Content source-lock audit; marker resolution; route publication — separate charters. Narrow claim approval does not authorize any of the above.

claims.statement: The English term 'bisulfide' has a lexical entry in Merriam-Webster.
claims.notes: Establishes English-language lexical existence of 'bisulfide'. Supports spelling boundary thesis.

claims.statement: The English term 'sulfide' has a lexical entry in Merriam-Webster.
claims.notes: Establishes English-language lexical existence of 'sulfide'. Supports the broader -ide/-id suffix pattern discussion.

claims.statement: The German term 'Sulfid' has a lexical entry in Duden.
claims.notes: Establishes German-language lexical existence of 'Sulfid' in an authoritative German dictionary. Supports the -id suffix form as a documented German-language standard.

claims.statement: The term 'bisulfite' refers to a distinct compound from 'bisulfide', as confirmed by a separate Merriam-Webster entry.
prohibited_uses: using bisulfite data as bisulfide data
claims.notes: Supports the core disambiguation rule: bisulfite is NOT bisulfide. Bisulfite data must never be used as bisulfide data.

claims.statement: The term 'hydrosulfides' has an entry in the IUPAC Gold Book chemical nomenclature standard.
claims.notes: Establishes IUPAC nomenclature authority for the hydrosulfide term. Supports the naming relationship between hydrosulfide and bisulfide.

claims.statement: Bisulfid appears as a German technical usage term in sulfur/water-quality monitoring context.
prohibited_uses: public proof of preferred German IUPAC spelling
claims.notes: Candidate usage claim only. Not approved for publication. Stronger source-locking required before removing source-required markers.

claims.statement: Duden records Oxid as a German lexical entry.
claims.notes: Candidate lexical support only. Does not approve a universal German -ide to -id rule.

claims.statement: Duden records Chlorid as a German lexical entry.
claims.notes: Candidate lexical support only. Does not approve a universal German -ide to -id rule.

claims.statement: Duden lexical entries for Sulfid, Oxid, and Chlorid provide candidate support for presenting these German -id forms as a cautious lexical comparison set.
claims.notes: This claim may support a cautious lexical comparison only. Stronger nomenclature or educational source required before public wording can state a general rule.

claims.statement: IUPAC inorganic nomenclature material provides English-language context for -ide naming in inorganic chemistry where directly supported.
claims.notes: English nomenclature context only. Not a German source.

claims.statement: Selected German academic teaching references describe or illustrate the -id ending in inorganic nomenclature contexts, supporting cautious draft review of forms such as Chlorid, Oxid, and Sulfid.
claims.notes: Candidate academic teaching support only. This claim does not approve public wording that states a formal German suffix rule.

claims.statement: Molybdän(IV)-sulfid has a German Lexikon der Chemie dictionary entry on Spektrum.de that supports cautious terminology framing for the de_core_mos2 route within the registered narrow dictionary-entry boundary.
